intentSnapshot.title: [Maintenance continuation] Database readiness with corrected test harness
intentSnapshot.body:
Delivery Execution: development-test

## Maintenance continuation, not a contract rewrite

Continue the operational readiness need observed after accepted ownership
delivery #1. This is a new run replacing cancelled maintenance Intent #8.
Preserve all prior artifacts, branches, PRs, accepted volumes, and evidence.
The ownership baseline remains main commit
`a2004d37bab5d4dbc758f3bdf9599547b4a45ad0`; no readiness production code merged.

## Observed evidence and failed attempt

An isolated replica of accepted ownership image
`ghcr.io/huangyingting/ai-native-sdlc-discovery-demo-it-service-desk@sha256:09bf8f338aaccaacb0290eafc6fe65c7f917cd8642688406aef93d24b0eb36a2`
with `SERVICE_DESK_DB_PATH=/dev/null/service-desk.db` returned health 200
`{"status":"ok"}`, dashboard 500, and readiness 404. This was deliberate fault
injection, not a production outage. No accepted volume was attached.

Maintenance #8 reached implementation PR #14, but real Green validation failed
(local 44 pass / 4 fail; Stage CI 36378117293 attempt 2 failed). The frozen tests
had two harness defects hidden by missing-route Red: returning a mock function
from `beforeEach` made Vitest invoke it as cleanup, and an existing SQLite
observer connection retained stale `SELECT *` column metadata after migration
on another connection. Independent reproduction showed schema refresh/reopen
resolves the latter. The run was cancelled rather than rewriting frozen tests
or weakening production code/checks.

## Explicit product outcome

Preserve `/api/health` exactly: HTTP 200 with `{"status":"ok"}`, independent of
database availability. Add separate Node.js `/api/ready`, dynamically evaluated
on every request through existing `getTicketStore().summary()`.

- Success: HTTP 200 with exactly `{"status":"ready"}`.
- Initialization or summary-read exception: HTTP 503 with exactly
  `{"status":"unavailable"}` and one fixed, bounded generic readiness-failure log
  message. Neither response nor log may expose error text, paths, ticket data,
  credentials, or stack traces.
- Both readiness outcomes include `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- A later request must re-evaluate and reflect repaired storage, without cached
  failure or success.
- Reuse the current accessor unchanged: its singleton is assigned only after
  successful construction. No second store abstraction or standalone SELECT 1.
- Existing first-use schema creation, nullable ownership migration, and seeding
  are allowed. Subsequent probes must preserve all persisted rows/fields.
- Preserve all 37 existing baseline tests, ownership and other application
  behavior, health, dependencies, shared automation, and earlier run records.

## Grounded testing and approval

Use existing direct-module Vitest conventions, not an invented HTTP harness.
Create one new readiness test file with all required deep assertions before
Implementation: exact bodies/status/headers; accessor and summary invocation;
init/read failure; generic sanitized logging; failure-to-success; successive
reads; dynamic route; real isolated file-backed repair, migration, seeding and
complete-row non-mutation; unchanged liveness and existing behavior.

Before the route exists, each named scenario must assert route existence inside
its own test body before guarded dynamic import. No import, collection, hook,
startup failure or skip counts as controlled Red. Record every and only
actually observed assertion-failing name in this run's expected-failure manifest.

Fix the identified test harness causes in the NEW unapproved test file:
`beforeEach` must use a block with no returned mock/cleanup value; observe
post-migration persisted data through a fresh read-only connection or explicit
schema refresh. Close all test-owned handles in cleanup.

Review the deeper test bodies for lifecycle/observer defects before freezing.
An isolated, explicitly labelled pre-approval harness experiment may exercise
the tests against the unmerged candidate from PR #14 outside the Tests branch;
it is not stage Green, production delivery, or permission to add production
code to a Tests commit. All actual stage checks remain required.

## Delivery and runbook acceptance

Update the application README with exact liveness/readiness contracts, local
commands, generic failure diagnosis, private configuration inspection and
repair/restart, isolation warnings, and local-demo/non-production limitations.

After protected merge and publication, use the SAME immutable image digest in
separate healthy and fault-injected instances, never an accepted volume.
Observe healthy ready 200, faulted ready 503, no-store and exact bodies, health
200 in both, fixed sanitized failure logging, populated ownership rows unchanged
across repeated probes, and a working dashboard/ownership UI. Verify documented
repair/restart. Only then submit digest-bound development-test acceptance.

## Scope and non-goals

This retains the product scope of #8: readiness, tests and related runbook only.
Do not change approved ownership behavior/tests, previous lifecycle artifacts,
shared automation, dependencies, infrastructure, authentication, metrics,
alerting, or review policy. No production incident, customer benefit, SLO,
availability certification, independent Human review, or Demo Ready claim.

Alternatives: retain manual dashboard checks (no dedicated routing signal), or
repurpose health (breaks liveness compatibility). A separate endpoint is the
explicit choice. Raise consequential contradictions rather than silently
changing it; no product choice is intentionally unresolved.
